hero_ceiling_lattice.notes:
Final 2 targeted fixes for hero_ceiling_lattice. ENABLED is still False. Name, pivot, bbox, col() and the frame ring geometry are unchanged. 5730 tris (budget 6000), QA hard fails 0.

What changed:
1. Backlit panel colour. The four peach materials (GL/GM/GB/GD) are replaced by a 7-level amber-gold ladder, M_AK_HLatticeGlow0..6. Emission colours run from #FFA010 to #FFA400 at strengths 0.30 to 1.36, over a near-black base colour so room and studio light cannot wash it to cream. I calibrated the values against the AgX Medium High Contrast transform with a test render of emissive patches. Measured in the bottom view:
   - centre cells: bright pixels ~#E4A863, mid tones ~#BD7E2B
   - rim cells: bright pixels ~#D7964A
   - earlier peach version, for comparison: bright ~#E9B173 with mid tones too close to the bright ones (the flat look)
   Under this transform AgX lifts blue as brightness rises, so a fully saturated #F0A040 core is not reachable with plain emission. The core lands a little paler than #F0A040, but clearly amber rather than peach.
2. Shading inside each triangle. Each cell now has four insets. Every edge is set in from its bar by t0 + tsh * max(0, n . SHADOW), with a constant SHADOW direction (0.5, -0.866). The core leans to the lit side and each triangle falls off into its bars' shadow, as in the reference zoom.
3. Radial falloff. The inset levels go up two steps at the panel centre, one step in the middle ring and none at the rim (RADIAL = 0.42 / 0.78).
4. Side view from slightly below. The insets are sunk between the bars (INSET_Z -0.023). The kumiko side faces use a new backlit amber-wood material, M_AK_HKumikoLit (emit 0.24, #FF9420). The low side view now reads as a glowing lattice field instead of a dark field with gold dots.
5. Timber. hero_shared.py appeared partway through this round and overrides M_AK_Timber with T_AK_HTimber, whose grain runs along U. This module's builders lay the grain along V, so the shared texture's grain ran across every member. Fix: Acc.emit swaps (u, v) on M_AK_Timber faces, and GU is now 1.0 (the old value of 7 compressed the kit's broad streaks). The grain now runs along the rails, posts and kumiko.
6. Worn arris. M_AK_HTimberEdge is now a subtle copper-red (#401C11, roughness 0.78). It is also on the two kumiko chamfers.

Other details:
- Diffuser clipping now uses half-plane clipping, with collinear-point cleanup. A first pass produced one zero-area face; that is fixed and QA is clean.
- Backup of the fix-3 module: WorkFiles/armory/hero/previews/hero_ceiling_lattice/final2/hero_ceiling_lattice_f3_backup.py.
- The from-below sheets use the existing work script WorkFiles/armory/hero/previews/hero_ceiling_lattice/below.py. preview_hero.py only shows the piece from above and the side.
- No textures were added. build_armory_kit.py, layout.json and ArmoryKit.blend were not touched.
- The scratchpad is shared with another agent (my first samp.py there was overwritten), so my scratch files are named lattice_*.
open_issues: Within-cell shading is 4 flat emission steps, not a true smooth gradient. At the corner close-up zoom the steps read as crisp bands; a smoother falloff would need either more insets (tri budget: 270 left of 6000) or a new per-cell glow texture (T_AK_HLatticeGlow_*), which needs a new tex_ script (not in this task's file list).

The M_AK_HTimberEdge chamfers on the rail underside are 11 mm wide, so the copper-red arris reads as a visible band in the very close slot close-up. At normal distances it is a thin worn edge. Narrowing the chamfers would change the profile geometry.
The core reaches about #E4A863 to #E6A355 under AgX Medium High Contrast rather than exactly #F0A040, because AgX lifts blue as emission brightness rises. It reads amber-gold, not peach.

The SHADOW direction is fixed in the panel's local frame; layout() may rotate some lattice panels, so neighbouring panels could show the bar shadows falling in different directions. Check in the context sheet or set SHADOW per placement if the user wants one global light direction.

hero_banner_coffer.notes:
COFFER COVE: The old LED strip sat on the lip's top edge, lit a shallow 5 cm soffit and read as a flat saturated orange band. The new cove profile (COFFER_PROFILE) works like this:
- The soffit lip now has an upstand (top at -0.090). The LED line is 1.4 cm wide and tilted 45 degrees up, in a trough behind the upstand, with its top 4 mm below the upstand's top. There is no line of sight to it from below.
- The line lights a deep stepped cove: an upper soffit at +0.045, a riser, a lower soffit at +0.030, and the moulding's outer face down to the upstand's shadow line. Because the cove is 14 cm deep, the light spreads across the wood instead of making one hot stripe. It is brightest by the lip and fades inward and down, and the grain shows in the lit wood.
- M_AK_HCoveLED is now a less saturated ~3000 K warm white (emit_color #FFCF9C, strength 130), so the amber comes from the lit timber.
- Coffer bbox and col() are unchanged; 288 tris.

JOINT (SM_AK_H_Ceiling_Joint): now a chunky two-tier cross-lap of laminated boards with vertical kerf splits and vertical grain:
- Tier 1 is a beam cap (half-size 0.205 x 0.190) lapped over a rib cap (half-size 0.145 x 0.255). Both stand 6.5 cm proud of the beam and rib side faces, and each runs about 6 cm past the other.
- Tier 2 is a bevelled 0.23 x 0.27 m block under the crossing.
- The caps stand 3.4 cm and 4.9 cm below the beam soffit, and tier 2 stands 7.8 cm below it.
- The tops (-0.160 / -0.162) sit in the coffer lips. They were deliberately offset by 2 mm: the first try had both caps' centre vertices on the same spot, which failed QA (no_coincident_vertices); it passes now.
- 360 tris, 3 UCX boxes. Placement via instances() is unchanged.
- The downlight is unchanged.

TIMBER UVs: hero_shared.py now loads during previews and overrides M_AK_Timber with T_AK_HTimber, whose grain runs along U. The old texture ran along V, so I swapped U and V:
- sweep_rect and prism_x: U now runs along the side and the plank.
- sweep_block: U runs down the joint's sides, and the end faces put U along the block's longer side.
Without this, the plank and cove grain ran across the members.

BANNER: checked with the shared agent's new T_AK_HBanner (M_AK_Banner not touched). The emblem is round and the side lines run up the sleeve. The top border strip, which is mapped onto the texture's side-line column, lines up with the side lines. The folds and sheen read correctly, so there was no geometry change: 1980 tris, same bbox.

OTHER:
- ENABLED stays False. QA hard fails are 0 on all 4 pieces.
- Assets/Armory/Hero/hero_banner_coffer.blend was saved by the assembly run.
- The key-view helper is closeup2.py in final2: a copy of the earlier closeup.py plus --plain, --emit (for tuning only; the final renders use the module's values) and --sheet.
- The coffer renders use the hero_shared plain Beam_4/Rib_2 ("H:" pieces, listed in final2\pieces_coffer_h.txt).
- A backup of the module from before this round is final2\hero_banner_coffer_before_final2.py.
open_issues: The 45-degree lip on the moulding's outer edge sits below the upstand's shadow line. It gets only bounce light, so it doesn't show the thin bright edge line the reference sheet has. A concealed LED can't light it directly without being visible from below, so I left it physically correct.

Under the preview's key light from below, the bottom faces of the beams, ribs and joints look greyish. That is the glossy HTimber catching the studio area light, and it looks the same on the shared agent's beams. It is the lighting, not the geometry.

The coffer and joint grain direction now assumes T_AK_HTimber (grain along U). If hero_shared's M_AK_Timber override is not adopted, the old T_AK_Timber (grain along V) would run the plank and cove grain across the members again.
In Unreal, the cove wash depends on Lumen picking up the emissive line (or a matching rect light in lights()). The Cycles previews show the intended look.
